steps.name: QC, reconcile samples, and run DESeq2 DE
caveats: counts.csv has 7 sample columns but metadata.csv has 6 rows — resolve this mismatch explicitly (extra/mislabeled sample) rather than silently dropping or guessing an assignment

With n=3 per group, dispersion estimates are noisy; rely on DESeq2's empirical Bayes shrinkage (do not disable it) and do not apply an additional ad hoc fold-change filter beyond what the acceptance criteria specify
Do not assume paired design — treat as unpaired per the stated experimental design
steps.question: Which of the 12000 genes are differentially expressed between treated (n=3) and control (n=3) liver samples in this unpaired single-batch design, using raw Salmon gene-level counts?
acceptance_criteria: Sample IDs in counts.csv columns are matched to metadata.csv rows; any count-matrix sample with no metadata entry (the counts file has 7 columns vs 6 metadata rows) is reported and excluded, leaving the intended 3 vs 3 design
Raw counts are modeled with DESeq2 (design ~condition), independent filtering and BH FDR applied
Output table includes gene symbol, baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj for all tested genes

A summary reports counts of genes at padj<0.05 and padj<0.1, plus a diagnostic (PCA or sample-distance heatmap, and dispersion plot) checking for outlier samples or batch structure within the single stated batch
MA plot and volcano plot are generated for visual QC of the DE call

steps.name: Power and precision assessment for the n=3 vs n=3 design
caveats: Do not present a post-hoc power number as if it were a pre-registered power calculation — frame it as a retrospective precision/sensitivity check on this specific dataset
Leave-one-out with n=3 per group means each LOO fit has only n=2 in one arm; report this explicitly as a stability heuristic, not a formal statistical test
steps.question: Given the observed gene-wise dispersion and effect-size distribution from the 3-vs-3 DESeq2 fit, what minimum effect size is reliably detectable at this sample size, and how much false-negative risk does n=3 per group carry for this liver drug-treatment comparison?
acceptance_criteria: Report the empirical relationship between mean expression, dispersion, and statistical power at n=3 per group using the fitted DESeq2 dispersions (e.g., via a power-simulation approach such as RNASeqPower-style calculation or bootstrap subsampling of the observed data)
State, in concrete terms, the minimum log2 fold-change detectable at 80% power for genes at low/median/high mean count, given the observed dispersion range
Quantify sensitivity to a single sample swap or outlier by a leave-one-out re-run of the DESeq2 model (drop one sample per group at a time) and report how much the significant gene list changes
Explicit statement of the confidence level appropriate for the DE call: what can be claimed as robust vs what is exploratory only, tied to the n=3 constraint

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of the treated vs control DE genes
caveats: Confirm the WikiPathways human GMT file is present before running (it is: HGNC gene symbols, 2026.07.10 snapshot) — no substitution with a mouse/rat pathway set is valid for this human liver dataset
Gene symbol matching between the DESeq2 output and the GMT file must be case- and alias-consistent; report unmatched gene count
steps.question: Which WikiPathways human pathways are enriched among genes differentially expressed between treated and control liver samples?
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment (e.g., over-representation or GSEA using the DESeq2 stat/log2FC ranking) is run against WikiPathways human gene sets confirmed present in the reference store
Report includes pathway name, WikiPathways ID, gene overlap, and BH-adjusted p-value
If fewer than 10 genes pass padj<0.05 in T1S1, enrichment is run instead on the full ranked gene list (GSEA-style) and this fallback is stated explicitly
Findings are reported as gene-set-level associations only, not causal drug-mechanism claims

plan.title: Liver drug DE: 3 vs 3 treated-control + power check
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a bulk RNA-seq liver drug-treatment study with raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 7 samples) and a 6-sample metadata table describing an unpaired 3 treated vs 3 control single-batch design — one sample in counts.csv has no matching metadata row and must be reconciled before analysis. The analytical path is standard for a small-n unpaired count-based comparison: (1) QC and align counts to metadata, dropping any unmatched sample; (2) DESeq2 differential expression with the Wald test and BH-FDR, which is appropriate for n=3/group and count data; (3) an explicit power/precision assessment quantifying what n=3 per group can and cannot resolve (detectable effect size, dispersion-driven false negative risk) rather than treating DE output at face value; (4) pathway enrichment on the DE gene list against WikiPathways human gene sets to give biological context; (5) a synthesis step folding the DE results and the power analysis into a single confidence-qualified answer to the research question. No translational/PK/safety data is present, so no drug-target or biomarker tracks are added.
